summary: Focus and alternatives as side effects, after Chapter 5 of Charlow's dissertation. The Focus monad pairs a value with its set of alternatives; F-marking puts the alternatives in and "only" and "also" consume them. The monad laws; application; association of "only" with one focus and with two; selective association, where "also" and "only" each take their own focus; Reset leaves a focus unchanged, so selective association also holds across a scope island. A four-person model separates the nested, crossed and unselective readings. The second part replaces State.Set by the Reader.Set monad: an indefinite still survives Reset, a universal becomes a truth value, a pronoun is bound inside a sentence, and binding across sentences is lost. A three-reader model shows the overgeneration of the abstraction rule in example (5.39).

sources.citation: Charlow, S. (2014). On the semantics of exceptional scope. PhD dissertation, New York University.
sources.available: sections 5.4.1-5.4.4 (pp. 135-145) and 5.5 (pp. 147-159) read; sections 5.1-5.3 not read; section 5.4.5 read and not formalized

theorems.name: focus_monad_laws
theorems.source_claim: T1. The monad laws for the Focus monad [C Def 5.6, p. 139].

theorems.name: focus_application
theorems.source_claim: T2. [C Fact 5.4, p. 139]: application is ordinary on the values and pointwise on the alternatives.

theorems.name: only_printed_form
theorems.source_claim: The gloss used for "only" agrees with the equation printed in [C Def 5.10, p. 141] when the regular value is among the alternatives.

theorems.name: association_single
theorems.source_claim: T3. [C p. 141]: "only met JOHN" holds iff John was met and no other alternative was. Carries a distinctness premise the print does not state.

theorems.name: association_unselective
theorems.source_claim: T3. [C pp. 141-142]: with two foci, one "only" associates with the pair. Same premise.

theorems.name: selective_association
theorems.source_claim: T4. [C pp. 142-143]: "also" over the outer focus and "only" over the inner one; (5.27b) and (5.28b) are instances. Carries two distinctness premises.

theorems.name: focus_survives_reset
theorems.source_claim: T5. [C p. 144]: Reset leaves a focus tower unchanged.

theorems.name: layered_island
theorems.source_claim: [C p. 144]: the evaluated island is a program of programs.

theorems.name: selective_across_island
theorems.source_claim: T5. [C p. 144]: feeding the inner layer of the island to "only" gives the configuration of T4.

theorems.name: nested_true
theorems.source_claim: Four-person model: the nested reading of "also only introduced BILL to SUE" is true.

theorems.name: crossed_false
theorems.source_claim: Four-person model: the crossed reading is false.

theorems.name: unselective_false
theorems.source_claim: Four-person model: the unselective reading is false.

theorems.name: reader_set_monad_laws
theorems.source_claim: The monad laws for the Reader.Set monad [C p. 153].

theorems.name: reader_set_reset_indefinite
theorems.source_claim: T6. [C Fact 5.7, p. 154]: an indefinite's alternatives survive Reset.

theorems.name: reader_set_reset_universal
theorems.source_claim: T6. [C Fact 5.8, p. 155]: a universal becomes one truth value.

theorems.name: reader_set_binding
theorems.source_claim: T7. [C p. 157]: a bind-shifted indefinite binds a pronoun in its scope at any stack.

theorems.name: binding_lost_on_evaluation
theorems.source_claim: T7. [C p. 158]: after evaluation a pronoun in the next sentence reads the incoming stack.

theorems.name: no_binding_on_empty_stack
theorems.source_claim: On the empty stack that pronoun returns nothing.

theorems.name: abstraction_overgenerates
theorems.source_claim: T8. [C (5.39), pp. 150-151]: in the three-reader model the abstraction rule admits a function that makes "nobody read a paper" true while the wide and the narrow reading are false.

evidence: DRAFT for the author's review; not an accepted source-level verdict.
Properties are compared extensionally (the same individuals at the same worlds), so no extensionality axiom is used. The source uses set identity.
"only" follows the gloss under Def 5.10, not the printed equation; only_printed_form relates the two.

The steps from a set of properties to a set of individuals (pp. 141-143) need distinct alternatives to give distinct properties. The print does not state this. The theorems carry it as a premise, and the four-person model discharges it by letting worlds vary. No conclusion about the source is drawn.
Alternatives of an individual are restricted to a relation Alt; the source prints the sets without a restriction.
In the Reader.Set part truth values are booleans, negation is a relation and the pronoun returns nothing on the empty stack, as in Exceptional_Scope.v.
The overgeneration example starts from the set printed in (5.39a); states and assignment modification are not modelled.

Rooth's two-dimensional semantics as a separate system (Def 5.4, 5.5), doubly focused words, the two monads layered (5.4.5), disjunction (Def 5.20), Fact 5.9, the repair of Def 5.14-5.15 and the Binder Roof Constraint argument are not formalized.

determination_rationale: DRAFT for the author. The two monads and the continuation layer transpose directly; the passage from properties to individuals needs a premise the print leaves unstated.

artifact_classes.description: extensional comparison of properties in place of set identity; booleans as truth values; negation as a relation
